question: What’s happening here?
text:
She sent the gift because she preferred a truce to war. Ibn Kathir's reading is that, having seen the might of Sulayman's armies, she judged that fighting him would bring ruin on her people, so she turned to peaceful means, hoping he would accept a gift or a yearly tribute and leave them alone. She then turned to peace, reconciliation, submission and conciliation, saying: "Indeed, I am going to send to them a gift and see with what the messengers return." That is, she would send him a gift suited to him, and see what his answer would be; perhaps he would accept it and hold back from us, or impose a tribute we would bring him every year.

Ibn Kathir also notes that she understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people. Her test was to see whether he was a king or a prophet: if he accepts the gift, he is a king, so fight him; but if he does not accept it, he is a Prophet, so follow him.

sources.quote: ثُمَّ عَدَلَتْ إِلَى الْمُهَادَنَةِ وَالْمُصَالَحَةِ وَالْمُسَالَمَةِ وَالْمُخَادَعَةِ وَالْمُصَانَعَةِ، فَقَالَتْ:
sources.before:
صَ إِلَيَّ وَإِلَيْكُمُ الْهَلَاكُ وَالدَّمَارُ دُونَ غَيْرِنَا؛ وَلِهَذَا قَالَتْ: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا﴾ .

قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: أَيْ إِذَا دَخَلُوا بَلَدًا عنْوَة أَفْسَدُوهُ، أَيْ: خَرّبوه، ﴿وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَا أَذِلَّةً﴾ أَيْ: وَقَصَدُوا مَنْ فِيهَا مِنَ الْوُلَاةِ وَالْجُنُودِ، فَأَهَانُوهُمْ غَايَةَ الْهَوَانِ، إِمَّا بِالْقَتْلِ أَوْ بِالْأَسْرِ.

قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: قَالَتْ بِلْقِيسُ: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَا أَذِلَّةً﴾ ، قَالَ الرَّبَّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ .
sources.after:
﴿وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ أَيْ: سَأَبْعَثُ إِلَيْهِ بِهَدِيَّةٍ تَلِيقُ بِهِ وَأَنْظُرُ مَاذَا يَكُونُ جَوَابُهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ، فَلَعَلَّهُ يَقْبَلُ ذَلِكَ وَيَكُفُّ عَنَّا، أَوْ يَضْرِبُ عَلَيْنَا خَرَاجا نَحْمِلُهُ إِلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ، وَنَلْتَزِمُ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ وَيَتْرُكُ قِتَالَنَا وَمُحَارَبَتَنَا. قَالَ قَتَادَةُ: رَحِمَهَا اللَّهُ وَرَضِيَ عَنْهَا، مَا كَانَ أَعْقَلَهَا فِي إِسْلَامِهَا وَفِي شِرْكِهَا!! عَلِمَتْ أَنَّ الْهَدِيَّةَ تَقَعُ مَوْقِعًا مِنَ النَّاسِ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَغَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ: قَالَتْ لِقَوْمِه
sources.said: She then turned to peace, reconciliation, submission and conciliation, saying: "Indeed, I am going to send to them a gift and see with what the messengers return." That is, she would send him a gift suited to him, and see what his answer would be; perhaps he would accept it and hold back from us, or impose a tribute we would bring him every year.

sources.quote: She understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people."
sources.before:
layman, and said:

وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ

(But verily, I am going to send him a present, and see with what the messengers return.) meaning, 'I will send him a gift befitting for one of his status, and will wait and see what his response will be. Perhaps he will accept that and leave us alone, or he will impose a tax which we can pay him every year, so that he will not fight us and wage war against us.' Qatadah said: "May Allah have mercy on her and be pleased with her – how wise she was as a Muslim and (before that) as an idolator!
sources.after: Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "She said to her people, if he accepts the gift, he is a king, so fight him; but if he does not accept it, he is a Prophet, so follow him."
sources.said: she understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people.
